text:
m1 - DESIGN PROPOSAL, as promised, before any candidate. AND THE MECHANISM IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN EITHER OF US STATED, including me. My "13 cells compared against 13" was misleading and I withdraw that framing.

MEASURED: PRESENT-TERM SETS ARE UNIFORM WITHIN EVERY ROW.

  u0: 13 cells, ONE non-empty term-set (6 terms, with Sensory)
  u1: 10 cells, ONE non-empty term-set (5 terms)
  u2: 13 cells, ONE non-empty term-set (5 terms)
  u3: 10 cells, ONE non-empty term-set (6 terms)

The second "distinct set" in each row is the EMPTY set - external states, which never reach blend. So term availability varies ACROSS units and never WITHIN one. That follows from the absence conditions being UNIT properties: `sketch.sensoryTerms.isEmpty` and `specified.isEmpty` depend on the recall unit, not the node.

WHY THAT MATTERS: THE SOFTMAX WITHIN A ROW IS UNAFFECTED. Every source state in a row carries the same present-weight, so the offset is common and CANCELS in normalisation. Viterbi likewise - every path traverses every unit, so a per-unit offset is common to all paths. So source-versus-source comparison is fine, and my earlier framing implied a defect there that does not exist.

THE REAL DEFECT IS SOURCE VERSUS EXTERNAL, AND IT IS LIVE.

  source cell:   sum over PRESENT terms + functionPrior     <- shrinks when terms are absent
  external cell: externalFloor (+ externalMismatch)         <- FLAT CONSTANT, cost.scala:703-706
                                                               does not vary with term availability

So a unit we could measure on FEWER dimensions gets systematically CHEAPER source costs against an UNCHANGED external floor. On this fixture u1 and u2 sit at present-weight 3.200 while u0 and u3 sit at 3.350: the first pair's source cells are up to 0.15 cheaper relative to an external floor that did not move.

A UNIT WE COULD MEASURE LESS LOOKS MORE ANCHORABLE. That is the whole defect, and it is exactly what my d_ent experiment showed behaviourally - Stephen King, participant-less, gaining 0.2562 source mass.

PROPOSAL: MAKE THE BLEND A WEIGHTED MEAN OVER PRESENT TERMS, NOT A SUM.

  current:  sum over present of w_t * d_t                      + prior
  proposed: (sum over present of w_t * d_t) / (sum of w_t)     + prior

I want to be explicit that I ARGUED AGAINST THIS SHAPE an hour ago, when I called renormalisation "imputation by another name". I WAS WRONG, and the reason is the fixed comparison target. Renormalising a RESIDUE invents evidence because nothing external anchors it. Here the cost is compared against externalFloor, a FIXED CONSTANT - so a sum whose term count varies while its comparison target does not is precisely the ratio-of-sums defect we have spent the day removing from estimands, sitting in the cost model. A mean is the ratio-of-sums fix.

WHAT I HAVE NOT SETTLED, and will not guess:
  - it rescales EVERY cost, so externalFloor, externalMismatch, distortionPenalty and the function
    priors are all now in the wrong units and need recalibration. That is a bigger change than the
    one line, and the WOG suite's tuned weights were chosen against the sum.
  - whether the prior should be inside or outside the normalisation.
  - the golden moves, and so does every pinned estimand.

So this is a proposal and a measurement, not a candidate. I would like your view on the mean-versus-sum question before I touch anything, because if you prefer carrying support alongside the value instead - the MassRatio shape - that is a different implementation and I would rather build one than start both.
